newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ yield curve flattens at close on moderate flows.
newsitem.headline: NZ yield curve flattens at close on moderate flows.

text.p: New Zealand bond yields ended lower than their previous close on Wednesday although they lost some ground from the open.
The 10-year bond, which began with a rally of 10 basis points, finished eight points lower at 7.25 percent.

"There has been a bit of volume going through around that 7.25 percent level in the 06s...It looks like one player lost a large chunk of long bonds last night and has been covering those for most of the day. He paid the offer at the open," one dealer said.
The curve flattened throughout the day on moderate volume, with the shorter bonds developing a slightly more offered tone. They rallied three basis points.
Money market dealers said the day was very quiet, with 90-day bank bills trading a tight 7.44-7.48 percent range.
Most traders had positioned themselves ahead of key inflation data due on Friday.

The Reserve Bank is forecasting December quarter underlying inflation at 0.5 percent for an annual rise of 2.3 percent, while the market is more optimistic. A Reuters poll of economists showed an average expectation of a 0.4 percent quarterly rise, for an annual rise of 2.15 percent.
"The market is definitely long and looking for a good number on Friday. I think it has the potential to disappoint," one bill dealer said.

"If it comes in at 0.5 to 0.4, I don't think we do anything. We probably just sit where we are, maybe even just bounce back up a little bit, but I don't think it will go too far because most people will take it as an opportunity to buy.
"For the market to really carry on and continue to rally, I think we'll need to see the number come in at 0.2 to 0.3 percent," he said.
Figures in brackets compare against previous day's close
